parallelWitness.quote: 德遣使迎之，超不告母妻乃歸。

reviewRows.before: Murong Chao, his elder brother's son, whom he had summoned from Chang'an, now arrived.
reviewRows.after: Murong De had earlier sent for his elder brother's son Murong Chao in Chang'an. Chao now arrived.
reviewRows.sourceReason: The current wording restores the kinship and the two stages of the journey. The parallel in Jinshu 128 explicitly says that De sent an envoy to meet Chao. ‘Sent for’ leaves open whether De issued a formal summons.
reviewRows.currentChinese: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
reviewRows.historicalReplacement: De's nephew Murong Chao, whom De had earlier sought to bring from Chang'an, now arrived.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 兄子 explicitly establishes De’s elder brother’s son. 迎 can mean go to meet or fetch; summoned is too definite, so use sought to bring without deciding who traveled. Source: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
兄子 identifies Chao as De’s elder brother’s son. 迎 does not by itself establish the precise means, so the narrower reviewed wording avoids asserting a summons.

originalWitness.excerpt: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。

latestAppliedReview.reason: 其兄子超 makes Chao the son of De's elder brother, which the idiomatic field drops. The new text restores it and keeps 初 (the earlier summons) separate from 及是而至 (his arrival now). The father stays unnamed, and no date is added. I re-checked the earlier approval and the bindings match exactly.

reviewRows.before: Earlier, De had summoned his elder brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point he arrived.
reviewRows.after: Earlier, De had sent for his elder brother's son Chao in Chang'an. At this point Chao arrived.
reviewRows.sourceReason: The current wording preserves the elder-brother relationship. Jinshu 128 describes an envoy sent to meet Chao. ‘Sent for’ expresses the earlier action and naming Chao makes clear who arrived.
reviewRows.currentChinese: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。
reviewRows.historicalReplacement: Earlier, De had sought to bring his brother's son Chao from Chang'an; at this point Chao arrived.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: The earlier 迎 action precedes Chao's arrival. 'Sought to bring' is interpretive: 迎 may mean to go meet or fetch, and the precise method and any unsuccessful attempt are not established.

originalWitness.excerpt: 初，德迎其兄子超于長安，及是而至。

latestAppliedReview.reason: 兄 means elder brother, so 'brother's son' is too vague. 迎 here is De's earlier act of sending for Chao from Chang'an, which comes before 及是而至. 'Summoned' keeps those two stages apart, and nothing new is inferred. I re-checked the earlier approval and it holds.

reviewRows.before: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty within his realm, and raised by two degrees the rank of every son who was his father’s heir.
reviewRows.after: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince, proclaimed a general amnesty within his realm, and granted two grades of rank to each son who succeeded his father.
reviewRows.sourceReason: The current wording restores both the edict and the rank provision. 人爵二級 specifies the award to each heir and gives no initial rank for the recipients. ‘Granted two grades of rank’ preserves the award without assuming that every recipient held rank already.
reviewRows.currentChinese: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
reviewRows.historicalReplacement: He issued an edict naming Murong Chao crown prince and granting a general amnesty throughout the realm; sons succeeding their fathers were each granted two grades of rank.

historicalDecisions.decisionReason: 子為父後者 identifies sons succeeding fathers, and 人爵二級 grants each two grades of rank. Increase could suggest everyone already held rank, which the text does not say. Source: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。
子為父後者人爵二級 grants two grades to sons succeeding their fathers; an increase would imply an existing rank that the wording does not require.

originalWitness.excerpt: 乃下書以超為皇太子，大赦境內，子為父後者人爵二級。

latestAppliedReview.reason: The current text leaves out 下書 (issued an edict), 境內 (within his realm) and the grant 子為父後者人爵二級. The new text restores all three: a two-degree rise in rank for every son who was his father's heir, which matches the literal field. Chao's title as crown prince (皇太子) is kept, and no date or person is added.

scope: The existing current English was independently accepted. Three exact alternatives address a narrower wording question each.
